I build the demand engines that turn B2B spend into pipeline.

Fractional and interim CMO for B2B SaaS, FinTech and recruitment tech. 19 years leading marketing at Hays, Randstad, Marks & Spencer and Cigna. I take marketing functions that are busy but not converting and rebuild them around pipeline, unit economics and reporting a board can trust.

Book a 20 minute call → See the work
The Problem

Marketing that is busy is not the same as marketing that works

Most businesses that call me are not short of activity. They are short of a line between activity and revenue.

  • Sales say the leads are poor. Marketing say sales do not follow up. Neither side has the data to settle it.
  • CAC is climbing and nobody can say which channel is responsible.
  • The CRM reports volume, not contribution. Board reporting is a dashboard screenshot nobody trusts.
  • Enterprise accounts are the growth plan, but marketing still runs an SMB lead volume model.
  • The MarTech stack was bought over five years by four different people and none of it talks to the rest.
  • A marketing leader has left and the function is drifting while recruitment runs its course.

The short version

I have spent 19 years doing the same job under different titles: turning marketing budgets into pipeline that finance recognises. At Hays I was Global Head of Growth across 31 countries and 36 languages, and marketing-sourced share of enterprise pipeline went from 11% to 30% against a 350+ client account set. At Randstad I rebuilt digital and operations for 32 enterprise clients, cutting onboarding from 67 days to 30 and blended CAC by 29%. At KSeye I built an AI-driven demand engine on a £200k budget that lifted deal conversion 22% and organic leads 37% on flat spend.

I start with the funnel maths and the CRM. Not the brand, not the website. Almost every stalled B2B marketing function has a qualification problem or an attribution problem underneath whatever symptom is being reported. Fix that first and every other decision gets easier, because you can finally see what it costs.

Nine of my eighteen roles have been contract, fixed term, fractional or interim. Entering a function that is underperforming or leaderless and creating momentum quickly is the core skill, not a side effect.

Who I work with

  • Revenue
    £5m to £75m
  • Sectors
    B2B SaaS, FinTech and specialist lending, recruitment tech, staffing, MSP and RPO, B2B professional services
  • Deal shape
    £50k+ ACV, multi-stakeholder buying committees
  • Team
    An existing marketing team of 1 to 10, or a marketing manager who needs senior cover
  • Backing
    Founder led, PE backed and VC backed
Where I am not the right fit. Low-value consumer products with a single decision maker. I have not led a B2C function at senior level since 2019 and there are better people for it. If you need daily hands-on execution rather than direction, you need a marketing manager, and I will say so on the call.
Services

What I do

Four ways to engage. Most start with a diagnostic and move into a retainer.

01

Demand Generation

Most B2B demand generation problems are qualification problems wearing a traffic problem as a disguise. I rebuild the funnel around qualified pipeline rather than lead volume.

  • MQL to MQA qualification, agreed with sales in writing
  • Lead scoring, lifecycle logic, intent-triggered nurture and follow-up SLAs
  • UTM governance, campaign taxonomy and attribution inside the CRM
  • Channel mix reallocated on contribution, not on last click
  • CAC, LTV to CAC, payback and contribution margin reported monthly
+39% MQLs and +17% revenue in a declining market · Hays
02

Account Based Marketing

ABM fails when the platform is bought before the programme is designed, or when the account list is built without sales. I build the programme first.

  • Tier 1 to 3 account structure, sized and agreed jointly with sales
  • Buying committee mapping across five to nine stakeholders per deal
  • Intent as a trigger that fires an action, not a report nobody reads
  • Tier 1 playbooks with bespoke pages, assets and stakeholder messaging
  • Demandbase, 6sense, Apollo, Influ2, LinkedIn, Salesforce, HubSpot
Enterprise pipeline share 11% → 30%, opportunities up 5x · Hays
03

MarTech & RevOps

Most B2B stacks were not designed, they accumulated. The symptom is a three-day month-end that still cannot answer what marketing contributed.

  • Stack audit: installed versus configured versus actually used
  • Data layer, CDP, single customer view and CRM object model
  • Multi-touch attribution built into the CRM, MMM where spend justifies it
  • Reporting at board, exec, senior and team level from one source of truth
  • Agentic workflows that remove the spreadsheet tax from month end
Onboarding 67 → 30 days, operating costs down ~18% · Randstad
04

Interim CMO

When a marketing leader leaves, the function does not pause while you recruit. Senior recruitment takes three to six months. Interim cover fills it.

  • Stabilise first: campaigns running, agencies accountable, team directed
  • Diagnose what was working and what the departing leader left unfinished
  • Fix the two or three things producing most of the drag
  • Write the spec for the permanent hire and sit on the panel
  • Leave documented systems and playbooks, not knowledge in one head
£12M omni-channel media plan built in the first 21 days · Ladbrokes

Hays Enterprise pipeline share from 11% to 30%
Global Head of Growth · 2020–2023
31 countries · 36 languages · 350+ enterprise clients · team of 16 · £750k media at 15% of revenue

Context

Hays is one of the largest recruitment businesses in the world. I joined as Head of Digital UK and progressed to Head of Digital EMEA and then Global Head of Growth, expanding scope from a single market to 31 countries and 36 languages.

The problem

Revenue and market share were declining. Marketing was running a lead volume model designed for a transactional business against an enterprise account set that buys in committees over long cycles. The MarTech estate could not report contribution at account level, so nobody could show what marketing was worth in the accounts that mattered most.

What I did

  • Built a global Tier 1 to 3 ABM programme against the 350+ client addressable set, integrating Demandbase, intent data, LinkedIn, Salesforce and custom lead scoring. Ran the ABM RFP covering Demandbase and 6sense.
  • Rebuilt the MarTech architecture: Salesforce, Tealium CDP, Liferay DXP, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Google 360, lead scoring, SEMRush and Hotjar, improving testing, lead tracking, attribution, single customer view and reporting at board, exec, senior and junior level.
  • Led a 36-domain URL migration with full content rewrite, CMS upgrade and SEO overhaul, alongside a Liferay replatform and rebrand across all 31 countries.
  • Repositioned the brand: ICPs, value propositions, creative, GenAI thought leadership, social listening, PR and awareness campaigns, with a change and internal comms programme securing rollout across all divisions.
  • Ran the Client Management and Solutions division, building ABM automation and upsell and cross-sell workflows with product and CSM teams.

Results

Marketing-sourced share of enterprise pipeline11% → 30%, plus 30% influenced
Contribution to new ARR target60%
New enterprise opportunities5x
Net revenue retention across 350+ clients119%
Revenue from existing accounts+45%, profit +89%
MQLs+39%, and +47% vs prior year on Salary Benchmark — highest in company history, delivered in the first six months
Revenue growth+17% in a declining market
CAC−16% while paid media grew £350k → £750k. ROAS +12%. LTV:CAC +19%
Organic traffic+90%
NPS14 → 29 within six months
Contribution margin52% → 77%

What transfers

The pipeline share number is the one most ABM programmes never move. It moved because the account set was agreed with sales before anything was built, and because intent triggered an action in the CRM rather than a report nobody read.

Randstad Enterprise onboarding cut from 67 days to 30
Global Head of Digital & Operations · 2023–2024
NAM, EMEA and APAC · 32 enterprise clients · team of 18 · £500k at 20% of revenue

Context

Randstad's enterprise business ran performance marketing and ABM campaigns on behalf of 32 enterprise clients, targeting £1m+ ACV named accounts and MSP relationships across three regions.

The problem

Onboarding a new enterprise client took 67 days. Every one was bespoke and rebuilt the same infrastructure from scratch. That is 67 days of cost before any revenue, multiplied across a growing client base. Sales cycles were also 67 days, and time to a qualified opportunity on ABM accounts was running at nine months.

What I did

  • Rebuilt the infrastructure as a repeatable model: CDP, CRM, CMS, tag management and integrations scoped once and configured per client, so onboarding stopped being a build.
  • Restructured 18 people across three regions around platforms, integrations, data and campaign operations, with onboarding playbooks, governance documentation and process frameworks.
  • Reshaped ABM to engage buying committees earlier through intent-driven personalised campaigns, GenAI content and pitch deck playbooks.
  • Deployed AI workflows across Salesforce, HubSpot, LinkedIn and Demandbase automating market and prospect analysis, case study generation, pitch decks, lead scoring and onboarding.
  • Architected a data roadmap covering CDP, single customer view, AI and Tableau BI, delivering KPI dashboards across sales, marketing and operations.

Results

Client onboarding67 → 30 days, a 56% reduction
Sales cycles67 → 30 days
Time to opportunity on ABM accounts9 months → 6
Closed-won rate+22%
Blended CAC−29%, ranging 16% to 47% by channel. LTV:CAC improved ~40%
Conversion+23%
CTR and ROAS+19% and +15%
Operating costs~18% lower
Contribution margin63% → 74%

What transfers

Onboarding time is a marketing metric that most marketing leaders never look at, and in any business serving enterprise clients it is often the largest recoverable cost in the funnel. It also compounds: the same infrastructure work that halved onboarding halved the sales cycle, because both were waiting on the same missing data layer.

KSeye AI-driven demand engine on a £200k budget
Head of Marketing · 2025–2026
Specialist lending / FinTech · £200k at 13% of revenue — the leanest ratio of three consecutive leadership roles

Context

KSeye is a specialist lender. The marketing function needed measurable pipeline against a small budget, in a regulated sector, with a long verification cycle and a broker-influenced buying process.

The problem

At 13% of revenue, nothing could be bought at scale. Any growth had to come from qualification quality and operational efficiency rather than media weight. The incumbent agency was not built for that.

What I did

  • Took end-to-end ownership of HubSpot as the GTM engine: lead scoring models, lifecycle stage logic, nurture workflows and sales system integrations.
  • Redesigned qualification from MQL to MQA, moving qualification to account level, with structured sales follow-up SLAs behind it.
  • Built agentic workflows in HubSpot Breeze and Make.com modelling lead propensity, risk profile and deal velocity across the full funnel.
  • Built an AI-driven ABM engine using intent data, custom GPTs, Apollo and LinkedIn, with Tier 1 account playbooks carrying bespoke landing pages, whitepapers and assets aligned to individual stakeholder pain points.
  • Built an AI-driven content and SEO programme using agents and Surfer SEO, with AEO and GEO citation techniques for AI answer engines.
  • Established UTM governance, campaign taxonomy standards and multi-channel attribution dashboards in HubSpot and GA4.
  • Terminated the incumbent agency, ran the replacement selection and rebuilt the partner set around AI and SEO capability.

Results

Deal conversion+22%
MQL to SQL conversion+19%
Organic lead volume+37% on a flat budget
Leads via SEO and GEO+34%
New partner opportunities3x
Contribution margin67% → 82%

What transfers

Small budgets force the right sequence. With £200k there is no option to buy your way past a broken qualification model, so the qualification work happened first and everything else compounded off it. The AI lift came from propensity modelling and content production at scale, both operational uses. It did not come from asking a model to make a strategic judgement.

Marks & Spencer International site launch cut from 12 weeks to 4
Head of Marketing / Ecommerce Manager · 2019
30+ international markets · team of 14 · contract

Context

M&S international ecommerce ran across more than 30 markets. I led a team of 14 across performance marketing, trade and content.

The problem

Launching a new country site took 12 weeks. Every launch was treated as a project rather than a process, which capped how many markets could open in a year and tied up a team that should have been trading. Channel investment was also allocated on last click, which systematically overpaid for the bottom of the funnel.

What I did

  • Built a scalable site rollout process, standardising the technical, content, localisation and trading workstreams so a launch became a repeatable sequence.
  • Launched media mix modelling, clickstream, attribution and LTV analysis to reallocate spend towards high-ROI channels, alongside new agencies, team structures, Adobe Analytics and Salesforce.
  • Led the Ireland platform migration from Demandware to Salesforce Commerce Cloud with zero disruption to live trading.
  • Improved the customer journey, on-site search and recommendation rules.
  • Rolled out international delivery and returns propositions: free returns and delivery, local and trusted returns, collection points and in-store refunds.

Results

Site launch time12 weeks → 4, saving £700k a year
Capacity releasedFive unplanned country sites delivering £1.4M incremental revenue
Revenue and ROAS+29% and +16%
Conversion and units per transaction+23% and +18%
Ireland migration£0.7m a year saved, zero trading disruption
Operating profit+£250k
India share of ecommerce5% → 8%
Team resultDouble-digit sales growth and £2m profit

What transfers

The £1.4M did not come from a campaign. It came from removing a process constraint and letting the team use the capacity that freed up. Operational speed is a growth lever and it rarely appears in a marketing plan.

Cigna New B2C proposition launched across 29 countries
Head of Ecommerce & Marketing · 2014–2015
Fortune 500 #90 · 29 countries · £4M project P&L · team grown 1 → 7

Context

Cigna was then the fourth-largest travel, health and life insurance provider in the US and UK, number 90 in the Fortune 500, with 35,000 employees. The business wanted to launch a direct-to-consumer proposition and roll it out internationally and through B2B partners including AA, RAC, Saga and Lloyds Banking Group.

The problem

A large insurer with no existing direct-to-consumer ecommerce capability, launching into a market where its partners already owned the customer relationship. No target operating model, no technology stack, no internal ecommerce culture.

What I did

  • Managed a £4M project P&L as project sponsor across BAs, PMs, development and customer service, holding decision rights on cost, risk and change requests.
  • Designed the target operating model, go-to-market plan, value propositions, user journey and customer experience for rollout to 29 countries and the B2B partner set.
  • Selected and negotiated the stack: Drupal CMS, quoting and claims engines, Eloqua, CRM, analytics, aggregators and affiliate networks.
  • Built a custom tracking, attribution and CRM solution to enable ROI and lifetime value measurement, which the existing infrastructure could not support.
  • Ran a change management programme embedding customer-first thinking, and grew the team from one to seven.

Results

Conversion rate2.7% → 4.8%, an 84% increase
PPC CPA£250 → £60, with sales up 200 units per month
CAC−40%, and −64% on the testing programme
Digital transformation savings£500k a year
Rollout29 countries plus AA, RAC, Saga and LBG

What transfers

Nothing worked until the measurement worked. The custom tracking and attribution build looked like a cost line at the start of the project and turned out to be the thing that made every subsequent optimisation decision possible.

We Are Aspire Five brands merged into one, +27% revenue a year
Head of Marketing (fractional) · 2016–2018
5 offices · 5 brands · team of 5 · 80+ sales staff · fractional engagement

Context

We Are Aspire is a recruitment group that had grown into five separate brands across five offices, each with its own website, positioning and marketing approach. This was a fractional engagement working directly with the Board, CEO and BDM Directors.

The problem

Five brands meant five of everything: five sets of SEO equity, five content programmes, five CRM configurations, and a sales team of 80+ with no consistent qualification model. Lead volume was measured. Lead quality was not.

What I did

  • Audited the business with the Board and delivered a rebrand merging five brands and sites into one.
  • Ran a MarTech transformation delivering real-time personalisation and single customer view on Segment CDP and Blueshift, with a full CRM overhaul.
  • Shifted lead qualification to an account-based model with intent-triggered ABM and CRM automation.
  • Built MQA-aligned lead tracking, scoring and pipeline dashboards with custom CRM workflows.
  • Upskilled 80+ sales staff on CRM, data enrichment, automated messaging and pipeline management.
  • Launched content and PR campaigns including the Digital Salary Guide, and renegotiated £60k across 16 job board contracts.

Results

Revenue+27% per annum, and +29% from enterprise accounts
Churn−34%
Candidate pipelines and MQLsDoubled. MQL to SQL +19%
Conversion7.49% → 19.42%, a 159% increase
Traffic and new customers+102% to 68k, +111% to 70k
Time to hire60 → 37 days
CPA+167% improvement on PPC, +94% on SEO
Digital Salary Guide campaign20k leads, 17k new customers
Cost savings£521k, plus £60k on job board contracts

What transfers

This was a fractional engagement of exactly the shape I now sell, so it is the closest analogue to what a client is buying. Two and a half years, board-level access, a rebrand, a MarTech rebuild and a qualification overhaul, delivered part time alongside a team of five. The brand consolidation was the visible project. The qualification model was the one that moved revenue.

How It Works

How an engagement runs

One day a week is the default. Some engagements run two. A diagnostic runs as a fixed-scope project first, so you can test the working relationship before committing to a retainer.

PhaseWhenWhat happens
DiagnoseWeeks 1–4Funnel, stack, data, team, agencies and unit economics reviewed, including interviews with sales rather than only marketing. You get a prioritised plan with a sequence, not a hundred-page report.
BuildWeeks 5–12Rebuild qualification. Fix attribution so channel contribution is visible in the CRM. Agree sales and marketing SLAs in writing. Rework the two channels carrying the most waste. First board report the leadership team actually trusts.
ScaleMonths 3–12ABM or demand programmes running to a repeatable cadence. Internal team mentored into more strategic responsibility. Agencies rebriefed against measurable outcomes. Forecasting models built so next year's budget is defensible.
Hand overOngoingThe aim is a function that no longer needs me. Usually a permanent Head of Marketing or Marketing Director hired and onboarded, with systems, playbooks and reporting already in place for them.

The two are not alternatives. A fractional CMO writes the brief and the agency delivers against it. I usually keep the incumbent agency and give them a sharper brief, because most agencies underperform on a poor brief rather than on poor capability.

FAQ

Questions people ask before the first call

What is a fractional CMO?

A fractional CMO is a senior marketing leader who works part time inside your business, usually one day a week on a retainer. They set marketing strategy, direct the internal team and agencies, and carry accountability for the commercial outcome. Unlike a consultant, they stay to implement rather than delivering recommendations and leaving.

How much does a fractional CMO cost in the UK?

My day rate is £750 for retained fractional work, which puts one day a week at around £3,250 a month. A permanent B2B CMO costs around £185,000 a year fully loaded once employer NI, pension, bonus, overheads and recruitment fees are included, which works out at roughly £845 per productive day after holiday and sickness are removed.

How is a fractional CMO different from a marketing agency?

An agency executes against a brief. A fractional CMO writes the brief. The fractional CMO sits inside the leadership team, sets strategy across the whole funnel and stack, directs agencies and is accountable for commercial outcomes rather than deliverables. The two are complementary, and most of my engagements keep the incumbent agency in place.

Is one day a week really enough?

For most businesses between £5m and £75m in revenue, yes, provided execution capacity exists internally or through agencies. The value comes from direction, prioritisation and unit economics rather than volume of hours. If daily hands-on execution is what you need, a marketing manager is the right hire and I will help you write the spec.

How long does an engagement last?

Typically six to eighteen months. Long enough to fix the qualification model, prove the change in pipeline, and build or hire the internal capability that eventually replaces the role.

How is fractional different from interim?

Fractional is one to two days a week on an ongoing basis, alongside two to four other clients, providing senior leadership at a level the business can afford. Interim is three to five days a week for one client, covering a vacant role for three to nine months, usually until a permanent hire is made. I take both.

Do you work on site or remotely?

Hybrid. I am based in Wembley, north west London, and work on site with London and South East clients for planning, leadership sessions and team mentoring. Remote first works fine elsewhere. I have run global remits across 31 countries and 36 languages, so distributed working is standard rather than new.

Will you replace our agency?

Usually not. Most agencies underperform because the brief is poor, not because the agency is. Improving the brief is cheaper and faster than switching, and I have run enough RFPs to know when a switch is genuinely warranted.

What happens in the first month?

A review of the funnel maths, the CRM, the MarTech stack, attribution, unit economics, team, agencies and budget, plus interviews with sales as well as marketing. The output is a prioritised plan with a sequence: where the biggest recoverable value sits, what to do first, and what to stop.

What sectors do you know?

Recruitment, staffing, MSP and RPO across seven years at Hays, Randstad, We Are Aspire and Hubbul. FinTech and specialist lending at KSeye, EVEN Card and Alpari. B2B SaaS at Pomelo Pay, Hubbul and Eagle Eye. Enterprise retail and insurance at Marks and Spencer, Signet and Cigna.

What size of business is too small?

Below roughly £2m in revenue there usually is not enough for a fractional CMO to work with. At that stage a strong marketing manager plus a short diagnostic project is better value, and I will say so rather than sell you a retainer.

Can you help us hire a permanent CMO?

Yes. Writing the spec, sitting on the interview panel and onboarding the successful hire is a normal part of exiting an engagement.
